note: The external legs' cost table (scripts/schedule.py pack-external), refreshed by PR from named runs. A tool priced per object (object_min) is cut into object legs of about target_leg_min each, longest object first; every other tool runs as one leg of job_min. Each leg's timeout is max(timeout_floor_min, ceil(timeout_factor x predicted)). A stale table costs balance and timeout margin, never results.

oorb.source: ESTIMATED, not measured on a hosted runner: the leg was off until the runner-fixes PR, so no hosted run has timed it. About 50 min is the full catalog's wall on 4 vCPU with the BC430 asteroid perturbers on (rows run as concurrent oorb processes, about 2 s per call); replace it with the first hosted job wall.

layup.source: job wall of run 39726274647, the only full run in which layup completed

jorbit.source: MODELED, not measured per object: no hosted run has completed jorbit over the catalog (it died after 41 to 72 min on runs 42506609035, 40612958887 and 39726274647). Each object is priced at the per-dt propagation times jorbit measured on run 40276519232 (Apophis, jorbit_time_ms: 8.8 to 11.6 s for |dt| <= 365 d, 32.9 to 34.1 s beyond) summed over the object's none-tagged propagation rows in run 42506609035's plan, plus 0.5 s per geocentric ephemeris row; the catalog sums to 205 min. setup_min is the measured Setup step (51 to 71 s); leg_overhead_min covers the import and the geocentre ephemeris.

orbfit.source: orbfit_time_ms per object, run 42506609035 (sum 42.3 min against a 43.7 min job; three objects hit the 600 s neofit2.x timeout). An object with no time failed at the fixture lookup and is priced at 0.01 min. setup_min is the measured image pull (34 to 85 s).
